$comment: Single source of truth for the container images that ship the MCP servers.
Dockerfiles and .github/workflows/build-images.yml. Adding a server means
Two strategies appear below, and the choice is forced by the dependency
merged  - the listed envs are resolved into ONE conda env. Only used
where a clean union solve was verified. Smaller image.
locked  - each env is installed side by side from its exact lockfile.
Required wherever a union cannot resolve: mace-torch pins
e3nn==0.4.4 while fairchem-core needs e3nn>=0.5, and the
generative envs pin torch versions that violate their own
declared constraints because no compliant build exists for
sm_121 / aarch64 / CUDA 13. Preserves the tested versions
exactly, which is the point: a container that resolves to
different versions than the environment you validated is a

images.name: lightweight
images.notes: No torch. fpocket has no linux-aarch64 conda-forge build, so the arm64 variant omits it and drug-pocket-detection must use its P2Rank path there.

images.name: mace
images.notes: torch 2.12 on both arches, resolved independently. Cannot host fairchem: mace-torch 0.3.15 pins e3nn==0.4.4, fairchem-core needs e3nn>=0.5 -- that conflict is architecture-independent.

images.name: fairchem
images.notes: arm64 pins torch 2.10.0 and overrides fairchem-core's declared torch~=2.8.0, because torch 2.8 has no sm_121 build. amd64 has no such constraint and resolves to the declared torch 2.8.0.

images.name: generative
images.notes: arm64 only for now. adit/diffcsp/mattergen were assembled by hand -- adit-agent's spec declares only python, pip and uv -- so unlike mace and fairchem their pip layer cannot be resolved from a spec and an amd64 lock must be derived from a built environment. torch-scatter/cluster/sparse are compiled from source here; x86_64 CUDA wheels do exist, so the amd64 build will not need that.
